title: Amar Singh v. State of U.P. and Others
court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
coram: Manoj Kumar Gupta and Prashant Kumar, JJ.
disposition: Disposed after withdrawal of theft recovery; fresh order under Supply Code.
headnote: Demand of Rs. 26,691 for alleged theft of electricity — department states the recovery stands withdrawn and that a fresh order will follow a hearing — writ disposed of with liberty to pass that order only by the procedure prescribed under the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005.
facts: Amar Singh challenged, before the High Court, a demand notice dated 11 January 2023 by which the electricity department sought recovery of Rs. 26,691 from him in a case of theft of electricity. The State of Uttar Pradesh and two others were the respondents. At the hearing, counsel for the electricity department stated that the impugned recovery had been withdrawn and that a fresh order would be passed after the petitioner was afforded an opportunity of hearing.

holding_units.topic: Fresh order after withdrawal of a theft-recovery demand
holding_units.holding: The writ challenging the demand notice dated 11 January 2023 for recovery of Rs. 26,691 in an electricity-theft case is disposed of on the department's statement that the recovery stands withdrawn, with liberty to the electricity department to pass a fresh order after hearing the petitioner and following the procedure prescribed under the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005.

principle_tags.application: Once the electricity department withdrew the theft-recovery demand, the Court disposed of the writ and left any fresh order to be passed only after a hearing and in accordance with the procedure prescribed by the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005. No clause of the Code was construed.

not_decided.point: Whether the petitioner was liable for theft of electricity and for the sum of Rs. 26,691
not_decided.note: The impugned recovery was withdrawn. The Court did not examine the assessment and left any fresh order to the department after hearing.
